commands: ls . rosterkit tests 2>&1 | head -50 && sed -n 1,40p rosterkit/$(ls rosterkit | grep -v __ | head -1) && ls tests | head -3 | xargs -I{} sh -c 'sed -n 1,25p tests/{}'
cat rosterkit/models.py rosterkit/errors.py; sed -n 1,15p tests/test_summary.py; cat Makefile

python3 - <<'EOF'
p="tests/test_seating.py"
s=open(p).read()
a=s.index("    def test_sorts")
b=s.index("    def test_bad")
new='''    def test_sorts_and_splits_rows(self):
        result = seat_rows(ROSTER, 2)
        self.assertEqual(result, EXPECTED)

'''
s=s[:a]+new+s[b:]
s=s.replace('''class SeatRows''','''ROSTER = [
    make("Halloway", "Juno"),
    make("Zane", "Omar"),
    make("Dunmere", "Piet")
]
EXPECTED = [
    "Row 1: Dunmere, Piet | Halloway, Juno",
    "Row 2: Zane, Omar"
]


class SeatRows''')
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF
make check 2>&1 | tail -5; make lint 2>&1 | tail -5; awk 'length>60' rosterkit/seating.py tests/test_seating.py; git add -A; git diff --cached

python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
for p in ("rosterkit/seating.py","tests/test_seating.py"):
    s=open(p).read()
    s=re.sub(r"\n\n\n+","\n\n",s)
    s=s.replace('"""Seating charts: students laid out in rows by last name."""','"""Seating charts: students in rows by last name."""')
    s=s.replace("    return (student.last_name.lower(), student.first_name.lower())","    name = student.last_name, student.first_name\n    return tuple(part.lower() for part in name)")
    open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF
awk 'length>60' rosterkit/seating.py tests/test_seating.py; grep -c '^$' rosterkit/seating.py; make check 2>&1 | tail -3; git add -A; git diff --cached --stat; git commit -q -m "Add seating chart rows by last name

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git log --oneline -1

trace.final_message:
I added `rosterkit/seating.py` with a function, `seat_rows(students, seats)`, and committed it as e085887. After the final edits, `make check` ran all twenty-nine tests and they passed.

- **Behavior:** It sorts students by last name, then first name, ignoring case. It returns one line per row, for example `Row 1: Dunmere, Piet | Halloway, Juno`. It raises `ValueError` when the seat count is zero or negative, or when the student list is empty.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_seating.py` has three tests. They cover sorting with row splitting, both bad seat counts, and the empty list.
- **Project rules:** Both files follow the line-length, function-length and blank-line rules. A `# ---` comment sits above the public function. I reviewed the staged diff before committing.
- **Late fix:** The first draft had double blank lines and a few lines over sixty characters. I fixed those before the commit.
- **Style gap:** Only one blank line separates the functions in `seating.py`, where PEP 8 asks for two. That follows the project rule against two blank lines in a row.
